text: Casper's core contributors just moved their first token standard KCC20 into its final review window. On October 7th, 2026, pull request 31 merges into Casper's own conventions repo and the status on the spec flips the last call, the final review window before standard goes final. Real tokens on Casper's base layer with every transaction enforced by the chain's own script rules not by an off-chain indexer. So let's get into how this is all playing out. Start with where this comes from. On June 30th, 2026, the Tokata hard fork gave Casper covenants. A covenant is a rule built into a coin that controls how it is spent and where it can go next. KCC20 is the shared rule book for a fungible token built from those covenants. Fungible meaning every unit is the same as every other. Four ideas. Idea 1. A common interface. Every KCC20 token carries the same state block, the amount, the owner, a few settings, and the same transfer or entry point. So any wallet, indexer, or app reads it the same way. Idea 2. Extended state. A token can carry its own data and behavior behind one digest, and transfers past that digest through untouched. Idea 3. Flexible authority. And this comes from KCC2. The owner of a token can be a public key, a key commitment, a script, or another covenant. So covenants can own tokens and govern them. Idea 4. Borrowed receive. Here's the thing. Every UTXO, every unspent coin, has to be funded with CAS. And a rule called storage mass makes tiny outputs expensive on purpose. So instead of a UTXO for every incoming token, the sender tops up one you already hold. Same owner. The CAS inside cannot go down. Only the token amount grows. Now CASPA already has tokens, KRC20, from CASPLEX, a third party control, live since September 2024. Around 2160 tokens by CASPLEX's own indexer count. It proved the demand. The difference is where the token lives. With KRC20, token operations are written onto CASPA as data, and the CASPLEX indexer works out who owns that. Your balance is the indexer's answer. With KCC20, the token state sits inside a covenant UTXO on the base layer, and the chain script enforces every transfer. Your balance is what the chain enforces. Savannah Helfer, the first listed author of KCC20, put it plainly back in June, a week before Tokata went live. That is the whole difference. On the KCC20 side, it is very early. Roughly 150 tokens by one community's tracker count. Think ERC20, enforced by the base layer itself. The timeline, straight from the repo. June 30th, Tokata activates. July 15th, the convention repo opens. August 20th, KCC1, KCC2, and KCC20 land as drabs. On September 22nd, the last call pull request for KCC20 opens. October 1st, KCC1, KCC2 move to last call. October 7th, KCC20 joins them. By late July, implementers were already reporting that their tokens only partly mashed a draft. So what's the bigger picture? Let's zoom out. After the September 22nd release, the main node code went quiet for three weeks. Then six commits landed in one week, October 13th to the 16th. Maintenance and plumbing, not a new feature. And Dagnyte, the next consensus upgrade, still has no date. Usage is a tiny base, around 82,000 standard transactions a day the week of October. Up around 22% on the week before. And the supply is fixed. Proof of work, no pre-mine. Around 96.7% of all Caspa is already mined. New demand meets very little new supply. Conditional, and that's the asymmetry I'm watching. And I'm telling you, this is going to be well worth the wait. At least for me anyway, nothing here is financial advice. But the high conviction holders, the ones who are in it for the long haul, are going to make it big time. Because the ones with the vision are the ones that will end up dominating the world. But I can tell you, if you're interested in stacking Caspa, while it's still cheap, the best way to do that is to get in on a bunch of good tokens that really are going to moon 100x, 500x within like six months to a year. I'm not talking about degen plays. I'm talking about investor back insider tokens that me and my group get in on early. We have a whole bunch of plays. Click the link in the description below. You can see all the receipts, 550x on NYX, 350x on the lab token, and many, many others. All investor back takes time. Sometimes it takes six months. Sometimes it takes a year before they pop. It's not like one of those like, I'm going to put in like 100 bucks on a degen play, and it's going 100x tomorrow. No, there's nothing like that. It's a strategy involved. Make sure you're surrounded by some like-minded people in a group of people who can share ideas. And everybody is in it for the money to all together, right? So we're all willing to help each other out and grow together. So click the link in the description below. And besides that, click that like button and that subscribe button. I'm going to catch you guys later.
